name: Visual Genome
description: Visual Genome is a dataset of 108,249 images with crowdsourced dense image annotations including region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. The first release uses images from the intersection of YFCC100M and MS-COCO, and all objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and question-answer pairs are canonicalized to WordNet synsets.
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
citeAs: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei. Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332v1.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. The first release uses 108,249 images from the intersection of YFCC100M and MS-COCO. Collection proceeded through multiple crowdsourcing stages for region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. Workers drew bounding boxes, wrote descriptions and QA pairs, extracted objects, attributes, and relationships from descriptions, and verified annotations. The dataset was collected over 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation, with approximately 800,000 HITs launched and over 33,000 unique workers contributing.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The first release of the Visual Genome dataset uses 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets. These are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded to Flickr by users.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Multiple descriptions for an image that referred to the same object were linked through co-reference chains. Scene graphs were created by combining region graphs and merging objects from different graphs when workers confirmed they referred to the same object; objects were considered candidates for merging when their bounding boxes had overlap over union of 0.8. All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and question-answer pairs were canonicalized to WordNet synsets using Stanford NLP tools, WordNet lexeme counts, hand-crafted mapping rules, and worker verification.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Descriptions and question-answer pairs were collected as freeform text. Stanford's dependency parser was used to extract nouns automatically as suggestions during object extraction. Stanford NLP tools were used to extract noun phrases from region descriptions and question-answer pairs for canonicalization. Attributes were normalized based on morphology (stemming). For relationships, prepositions were ignored for WordNet mapping and verb synsets were selected using matching sentence frames and root hypernyms. New region descriptions were programmatically checked with BLEU score thresholds of 0.7 against prior image-specific descriptions and the top 100 most common global descriptions to enforce diversity.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk annotated all components. For region descriptions, workers drew three bounding boxes and wrote three descriptions for enclosed regions; images were repeatedly sent to workers until 50 region descriptions were collected, with workers encouraged to avoid repeating prior descriptions. For objects, workers extracted all objects from each description and grounded each object with a bounding box, with suggestions from previously extracted objects and Stanford dependency parser nouns. For attributes and relationships, workers were shown a region description and its extracted objects and asked to add attributes to objects or connect object pairs with relationships, forming region graphs. Scene graphs were formed by combining region graphs and confirming co-referenced objects. For question answering, workers wrote freeform and region-based QA pairs following rules to start questions with interrogative words, avoid ambiguity and speculation, and ensure answerability from the image.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All data went through a verification stage. All components except objects were verified using majority voting by three unique workers, and an annotation was added if at least two workers judged it factually correct. Objects were verified using rapid judgments inspired by rapid serial visual processing to speed verification. Canonicalization mappings were also sent to Amazon Mechanical Turk for workers to verify and change to one of four alternative synsets if a better fit.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image has 50 region descriptions, an average of 21 objects, 16 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 question-answer pairs. Verification used 3 workers per annotation for majority voting.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers contributed. 93.02% of workers were from the United States, 1.29% from the Philippines, 1.13% from Kenya, 0.94% from India, 0.50% from Russia, 0.47% from Canada, and 2.65% from other countries. The majority of workers were between 25 and 34 years old. The gender split was 54.15% male and 45.85% female. The youngest contributor was 18 years old and the oldest was 68 years old.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford dependency parser; Stanford NLP tools (CoreNLP); BLEU score matching; WordNet synset mapping heuristics
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper refers to the first release of the Visual Genome dataset and notes that the crowdsourcing effort is ongoing. Further visualizations, API, and additional information can be found online. No explicit versioning timeframe, maintainers, or deprecation policy is provided.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotator demographics including country, age, and gender were collected and reported.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable the next generation of computer vision models for comprehensive scene understanding, including applications such as image search, question answering, and robotic interactions. The authors state that Visual Genome provides a broader understanding of the visual world by complementing object detection with abilities to describe objects and explain their interactions and relationships.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people. The authors also note that certain sports such as skiing and surfing are overrepresented due to a bias in the image set. Worker geography is heavily skewed toward the United States, with 93.02% of workers contributing from there.
rai:dataLimitations: The canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. Some descriptions contain no objects and therefore have no region graphs associated with them. The dataset is somewhat biased toward images of people, and certain sports are overrepresented. The paper also notes that current evaluation methods for question answering cause problems when answers are long phrases and sentences.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and benchmarking computer vision models for comprehensive scene understanding. The paper discusses use for attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region description generation, visual question answering, dense image captioning, image understanding evaluation, relationship extraction, and semantic image retrieval. The dataset is described as a general-purpose representation of the visual world without bias toward a particular task.
